settings.title: Frequently Asked Questions: White House AC & Cooling

items.item_title: How much does AC repair cost in White House, TN?
Do you offer emergency AC repair in White House?
Why is my air conditioner running constantly but not cooling the house?
Should I choose a heat pump or a central AC for my Middle Tennessee home?
How do I know if I should repair or replace my air conditioner?

settings.editor: Most standard air conditioner repairs in the White House area range from $150 to $450 for common issues like replacing capacitors, contactors, or clearing condensate drain lines. Larger repairs involving fan motors or refrigerant leaks fall higher on the scale. At Petitt Heating & Cooling, we provide upfront, flat-rate pricing before starting any work so you know the exact cost upfront.

Yes, we offer 24/7 emergency AC repair with same-day dispatch throughout Robertson and Sumner Counties. Under our Petitt Promise, existing customers are guaranteed an emergency response time within 12 hours or less if their cooling system fails during extreme heat.

An AC that runs non-stop without lowering the indoor temperature is usually caused by a clogged air filter, a dirty outdoor condenser coil, or low refrigerant levels from a system leak. Running a system low on refrigerant can overheat and burn out the compressor, so it is best to turn the system off and call a local technician right away.

Heat pumps are often the best choice for Middle Tennessee homes because they provide energy-efficient summer cooling and reverse their cycle to heat your home during our mild winters. While a standard central air conditioner only cools your home (requiring a separate gas or electric furnace), a heat pump handles both seasons in a single efficient unit.

You should consider replacing your AC if it is over 10 to 12 years old, requires frequent refrigerant refills, or if the cost of a repair equals more than 50% of a new system's value. Modern high-efficiency replacement units lower your monthly utility bills and eliminate the stress of unexpected breakdowns.
